description.value: The study examined changes in whole-brain functional connectivity following right inferior frontal cortex fMRI neurofeedback training in adolescents with ADHD, and assessed whether these changes were specific to the trained region and associated with clinical improvement.

design.value: A randomized controlled trial compared 18 ADHD adolescents receiving fMRI neurofeedback of the right inferior frontal cortex with 13 ADHD adolescents trained to enhance the left parahippocampal gyrus. The current study focused on functional connectivity changes from the first to the last neurofeedback run and used the control group to assess specificity.

description.value: Eighteen right-handed boys aged 12–17 years with ADHD who received fMRI neurofeedback to enhance the right inferior frontal cortex.

inclusion_criteria.value: Met the clinical DSM-5 criteria for the diagnosis of ADHD, combined hyperactive/impulsive and inattentive or inattentive subtypes.
Scored above clinical ADHD threshold on the Conners' Parent Rating Scale.

task_description.value: Boys were offered 14 fMRI-Neurofeedback runs, with each run consisting of seven rest blocks of 30 s and six activation blocks of 50 s. The rest blocks showed an underwater dolphin image and the activation blocks showed a video-clip of a rocket. Boys were asked to move the rocket towards space by any means they found helpful. Continuous feedback was provided every repetition time, about their brain activation in the target region of interest, with the direction and distance travelled in space proportional to their BOLD response.

instructions.value: you can try to concentrate on the rocket; try any other method that works for you

task_performance_measures.value: A score from 0 to 10 reflecting the percentage of distance travelled through space during each run.
A monetary incentive corresponding to the best performance in the session.

task_description.value: After the last fMRI-Neurofeedback run, a 5-min fMRI transfer run was conducted. This was identical to the Neurofeedback training runs, using the same stimuli, but without the feedback, and consisted of four rest and three activation blocks.

stimuli.value: The same underwater dolphin image and rocket video-clip stimuli as the Neurofeedback training runs.

description.value: The images were transferred to an external Linux workstation and pre-processed using AFNI. Effects of head motion were corrected for in real time. Native-space masks of the target ROIs and white matter reference region were created and applied to the pre-processed fMRI images to extract the mean BOLD signal in real time.

steps.value: Real-time transfer of reconstructed fMRI scans from the scanner hardware.
Creation of a native-space image mask of the rIFC and white matter reference region using the T1-weighted structural image and a two-volume echo-planar image localizer.
Extraction of the mean BOLD signal from each ROI for each newly acquired brain volume.

description.value: Offline fMRI data were processed to minimise motion-related artefacts, realigned to a template, and smoothed before functional connectivity analysis.

steps.value: Calculate a 3D volume consisting of the average intensity at each voxel over the whole experiment and use it as a template.
Realign each 3D image volume to the template using rigid body registration by combining rotations around the x, y, and z axes and translations in x, y, and z.
Smooth the data using a Gaussian filter at 7.8 mm FWHM.
Transform functional connectivity maps to standard space by rigid body transformation into a high-resolution echo-planar image and affine transformation onto a Talairach template.

model_settings.value: Pre- and post-fMRI-Neurofeedback effects on clinical measures were tested.
For each subject, the average time series over the whole ROI was used as a model for a whole-brain correlation analysis producing functional connectivity maps.
Group connectivity maps were computed by determining the median correlation coefficient across subjects at each voxel, to give more robustness against outlier effects.

Separate analyses tested positive and negative functional connectivity differences between the last (11th or earlier) and first fMRI-Neurofeedback run using Brodmann area 44 and Brodmann area 45 seed regions. A voxel-level p < 0.05 was followed by a data-driven cluster-level threshold giving less than one false positive cluster per whole-brain map.

estimator.value: randomization-based tests for voxel- and cluster-wise differences

model_settings.value: Run was the within-group repeated measure and group was the between-group measure; changes between the last and first run were compared between the rIFC-Neurofeedback and lPHG-Neurofeedback groups.
Absolute and relative mean displacement were compared between groups.

Exploratory correlations tested associations between functional connectivity changes and changes in primary and secondary clinical outcome measures; correlations between motion parameters and significant functional connectivity changes were also tested. Correlations were not adjusted for multiple testing.
